title: Inference Platform Economics — Fireworks, Together, Baseten, Modal, Replicate, Anyscale

questions.question: Which three market segments does the lesson use to organize 2026 inference vendors?
options: Free tier, paid self-serve, and enterprise contract — the pricing-page split, not the lesson's segmentation
Custom silicon, GPU platforms, and API-first marketplaces
Single-tenant, multi-tenant, and on-prem — a deployment split the lesson does not use to organize vendors
Open-source licensed, commercial closed, and hybrid — a licensing split the lesson does not use to organize vendors
questions.explanation: The lesson organizes the 2026 market into custom silicon (Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova), GPU platforms (Baseten, Together, Fireworks, Modal, Anyscale), and API-first marketplaces (Replicate, DeepInfra, OpenRouter, Fal).

questions.question: Around what sustained GPU utilization does per-minute billing (Baseten, Modal) start to beat per-token billing (Fireworks, Together)?
questions.explanation: The lesson's rule of thumb is that above roughly 30% sustained utilization of a dedicated GPU, per-minute billing starts to beat per-token; below that, per-token wins because you avoid paying for idle capacity.

questions.question: Which platform is described as Python-native serverless with per-second billing and 2-4s cold starts after pre-warming?
options: Modal — pure Python serverless, per-second billing, 2-4s cold starts with pre-warming
Baseten — Truss packaging with dependencies and secrets, per-minute billing on dedicated GPUs
Fireworks — FireAttention engine, per-token pricing, claims 4x lower latency than vLLM
Anyscale — Ray-native platform built on RayTurbo, tuned for distributed Python workload graphs
questions.explanation: Modal is described as true Python serverless: decorate a function with `@modal.function(gpu="A100")`, per-second billing, and 2-4s cold starts with pre-warming (under 1s for small models).

questions.question: What is Fireworks's notable LoRA pricing differentiator?
options: LoRA-served requests cost more than the base model, the premium most competing platforms charge
LoRA fine-tunes are not supported on Fireworks at all, only base models can be served
LoRA-served requests are charged at the base model's per-token rate, with no fine-tune premium
LoRA requests require a separate dedicated GPU contract outside the normal per-token pricing
questions.explanation: The lesson notes Fireworks serves a fine-tuned (LoRA) model at the same per-token rate as the base model, calling out that other providers typically charge a premium for LoRA-served requests.

questions.question: Which platform fits a regulated healthcare customer that needs SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA-ready posture, and dedicated GPUs?
options: Together — 200+ model catalog, open-source releases within days of upstream, breadth-optimized rather than compliance-optimized positioning
Anyscale — Ray-native distributed Python platform built around the RayTurbo inference engine
Replicate — pay-per-prediction multimodal marketplace for image, video, and audio models
Baseten — SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-ready, dedicated GPUs from T4 through B200, the common fintech and healthcare pick
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Baseten as enterprise-polish-optimized: SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-ready, dedicated GPU range from T4 through B200, and calls it the common fintech and healthcare pick.

questions.question: Why does the lesson argue that custom-engine claims are mostly marketing shade at the platform layer?
options: vLLM and SGLang represent roughly 80% of production open-source inference, so platform differentiation comes more from DX, attribution, and SLAs than the serving engine itself
Per-token pricing is the only real differentiator the lesson credits, since it treats FireAttention, RayTurbo, and Baseten's own inference stack as performing identically in every practical benchmark
All the custom engines advertised — FireAttention, RayTurbo, Baseten's stack — are forks of TensorRT-LLM repackaged under new marketing names
Custom engines like FireAttention and RayTurbo never outperform vLLM on any benchmark the lesson cites, regardless of workload
questions.explanation: The lesson states vLLM and SGLang represent about 80% of production open-source inference, so despite every platform touting a custom engine (FireAttention, RayTurbo, etc.), the real differentiation is DX, attribution, and SLAs rather than the engine itself.
